items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI is a different kind of GTA — so it needed a different kind of ending
items.raw:
In most Grand Theft Auto games, and most open-world games for that matter, the world is left open for you to explore once the credits roll. It could be Los Santos or a twisted take on Manhattan, but the idea is that the main story is just one part of the experience. After that's done, there are usually still places you haven't explored or side missions you left lingering. But Grand Theft Auto VI doesn't work quite the same way. Because of its storyline, which involves a couple trying to get out of the criminal life for good, that kind of ending didn't really fit.

The X11L is the best TV TCL has ever built, which is probably why it still starts at nearly $3,000. | Photo: John Higgins / The Verge	

Most of us spend a lot of time with our TVs, be it watching movies, TV shows, the news, or playing games. It’s part of being a fan of technology. And while they’re big purchases, they can last for years. But eventually, the time comes when we need a new one. Has that time come for you? Black Friday sales will make it easier to find something great for a lot less than it’d usually cost.
With several different types of TVs out there, it can get confusing which ones are worth it. Are the new RGB LED TVs all they’re cracked up to be? (Sometimes.) Does OLED still deliver the best contrast available? (Yup.) Are tried-and-true LED TVs still worth it in 2026 for those on a budget? (Absolutely.) One thing you can be sure of, is any TV I recommend here is more than worth the price. If you need a TV, Black Friday is the time to buy.

items.title: The absolute best Black Friday deals we’ve found (so far)
items.raw:
This year’s Black Friday deals have launched in waves over the past several weeks, but now the floodgates have officially opened. You can now take advantage of the lowest prices we’ve seen in-store and online for video games, wireless earbuds, TVs, e-readers, robot vacuums, and so much more. We can’t guarantee a deal you’ve had your eye on will last through Cyber Monday; however, if prior years are any indication, most will stick around through the long holiday weekend.
As usual, we sorted through thousands of deals to find the ones truly worth sharing, with an eye for the products and services we’ve tested here at The Verge. With prices up across multiple categories due to RAMageddon, some deals may not seem as big as in prior years. For example, Apple’s latest MacBook Air recently fell to its pre-price hike level for the first time since July. That’s a deal to us, and several other discounts are taking a similar shape. We’ll provide context when possible and keep this post updated throughout the day.

Despite having launched over a year ago, the Apple Watch SE 3 is still the Apple Watch model we recommend for most people. Heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding creating hazardous conditions for millions travelling for holiday
King tides and huge waves have been battering both coasts of the US during a turbulent Thanksgiving period, with severe weather threatening millions across the country. Dropping of corruption charges against Israeli PM after unusual intervention could set damaging precedent
The Israeli judges presiding over Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial have called on prosecutors to end proceedings, a highly unusual intervention that leaves the attorney general facing a momentous political decision.
The prime minister has been charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust in three complex and overlapping criminal cases that hinge on his relationship with telecoms magnates and other wealthy businessmen. Ending the trial without a ruling could set damaging precedents for media independence and how politicians are held to account.

items.title: French town divided over church bells ringing every 15 minutes at night
items.raw:
Longtime residents of La Garnache defeat newer neighbours in latest rural culture clash over ‘sensory heritage’
A ding-dong has divided the town of La Garnache in western France over attempts to silence the bells of the local church, which strike all night.
Since 1942, the clock tower of Notre-Dame de l’Assomption has chimed an eighth-century hymn every 15 minutes … day and night. Between 10pm and 7am, the bells ring 37 times, adding up to more than 700 individual chimes.

items.title: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
items.raw:
The Forerunner 265S is great for runners with small wrists. | Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge	

The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks of fitness watches at the time, and the only thing that bugged me was its price. But now that it’s down to $299.99 (a $150 discount off its MSRP) at Amazon and Best Buy for Black Friday, I can easily recommend it.
Garmin Forerunner 265S (42mm)
Garmin’s Forerunner 265S is identical to the standard 265, only it features a slightly better battery life and a smaller 42mm build for those with more petite wrists.

Where to Buy:

 $449.99 $299.99 at Amazon
 $449.99 $299.99 at Best Buy

The neat thing about Garmins in general is that you really don’t need the latest models to get the most out of the company’s platform. Its watches tend to get firmware updates for several years after launch, which is how long the average Garmin user tends to hold on to theirs. This particular watch is best suited for folks who want something a bit slimmer and smaller, enjoy a pop of color, and want a little extra fitness tracking prowess — but don’t need the whole kit and caboodle that sends the price up by hundreds.
There are a few other Garmin models I like that are also on sale during Black Friday. I wish that I had 10 arms to fully vet every single last one, but alas. That said, here are some others that I have tested and recommend:
The Garmin Fenix 8 is $749 at Amazon, Best Buy, and REI, which is a 25 percent discount off its original price. Its higher price comes down to having more features than the Forerunner 265S, so it’s really best for someone who does multiple outdoor sports and could make use of its handy LED flashlight.
Garmin’s Venu 4 is $449 at Amazon, Best Buy, and REI, an 18 percent discount. This is a great option if you’re looking for more of a smartwatch that does fitness than a fitness-y watch that looks like a smartwatch. It’s a fine line, but if you know, you know.
Finally, Garmin’s Forerunner 970 is $100 off, costing $649 at Amazon, Best Buy, and REI. This is what I’d recommend to marathoners who need something a bit more robust but not as heavy-duty as the flagship Fenix line. I’ve used it to train for a few races and it’s a solid upper-midrange (for Garmin!) option.

items.title: At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway
items.raw:
Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred
A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.
The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.

items.title: UN sacked Palestinian staff on back of unproven Israeli allegations, tribunal rules
items.raw:
Judgment casts doubt on evidence linking aid workers to Hamas and says humanitarian efforts in Gaza were damaged
A UN tribunal has cast doubt on the evidence used to justify the sacking of Palestinian UN aid workers in 2024, saying it was based “almost entirely” on unproven assertions from the Israeli government and had damaged humanitarian operations in Gaza.
The judgment, seen by the Guardian, raises fresh questions about the decision by the UN Relief and Works Agency (Unrwa), the main humanitarian organisation working in Gaza, to sack members of staff. It was taken on the basis of Israeli allegations of involvement in the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023.

items.title: Palestinian journalist killed by Israel in Gaza wins Rory Peck prize

Mariam Dagga, the Palestinian war correspondent who was killed at the age of 33 in Gaza in an Israeli strike, has posthumously won the prestigious Rory Peck prize for freelance video journalists, the organisers announced on Wednesday.
She shares the award with two of her colleagues from the Associated Press (AP), Abdel Kareem Hana and Jehad Alshrafi, “for their powerful coverage of the human cost of the war” in the Palestinian territory, the Rory Peck Trust said.
